meta.cover: Covers the key sections asked in the LLB Banking Law paper — not every section of the Act.

items.head: 'Banking' defined
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: The accepting, for the purpose of lending or investment, of deposits of money from the public, repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawable by cheque, draft, order or otherwise.

items.head: 'Banking company' defined
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: Any company which transacts the business of banking in India.

items.head: Forms of business in which banking companies may engage
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: Lists the permitted businesses — borrowing, lending, dealing in bills, cheques and drafts, guarantees, letters of credit, safe custody, agency business, foreign exchange, underwriting, and other business notified by the Central Government.

items.head: Use of words 'bank', 'banker', 'banking'
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: A company carrying on banking must use at least one of these words in its name; no other company may use them in its name.

items.head: Prohibition of trading
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: A banking company shall not directly or indirectly deal in buying, selling or bartering goods, except in connection with realising its security or bills of exchange held for collection.

items.head: Disposal of non-banking assets
items.group: Preliminary and business of banking companies
items.gist: Immovable property acquired in satisfaction of claims must be disposed of within seven years (extendable by the RBI).

items.head: Prohibition of employment of managing agents and restrictions on certain employments
items.gist: A banking company cannot employ a managing agent or persons whose remuneration takes the form of a share of profits, or who are insolvent or convicted of offences involving moral turpitude.

items.head: Board of directors to include persons with professional or other experience
items.gist: At least 51 per cent of directors must have special knowledge or practical experience in accountancy, agriculture, banking, co-operation, economics, finance, law, small-scale industry or other notified matters.

items.head: Banking company to be managed by whole-time chairman
items.gist: The company is managed by a whole-time chairman or managing director, subject to the board's superintendence.

items.head: Requirement as to minimum paid-up capital and reserves
items.gist: Prescribes the minimum paid-up capital and reserves a banking company must maintain.

items.head: Regulation of paid-up capital, subscribed capital and authorised capital and voting rights
items.gist: Subscribed capital must be at least half the authorised capital and paid-up capital at least half the subscribed capital; caps voting rights of shareholders.

items.head: Restrictions as to payment of dividend
items.gist: No dividend until all capitalised expenses (preliminary expenses, losses etc.) are written off.

items.head: Reserve fund
items.gist: Before declaring a dividend, transfer at least 20 per cent of profits each year to a reserve fund.

items.head: Cash reserve
items.gist: Every bank (other than scheduled banks covered by RBI Act S.42) must maintain a cash reserve as specified by the RBI.

items.head: Restriction on nature of subsidiary companies and holding of shares
items.gist: A bank may form subsidiaries only for permitted purposes and cannot hold shares in any company, as pledgee, mortgagee or owner, exceeding 30 per cent of that company's paid-up capital or 30 per cent of its own paid-up capital and reserves, whichever is less.

items.head: Restrictions on loans and advances
items.gist: No loans on the security of its own shares; no loans or advances to its directors, or to firms, companies or individuals in which they are interested, except as permitted.

items.head: Power of RBI to control advances by banking companies
items.gist: The RBI may determine policy on advances and give directions on purposes, margins, maximum amounts to any one borrower and rates of interest; banks must comply.

items.head: Rates of interest not subject to scrutiny by courts
items.gist: A transaction between a bank and its debtor cannot be reopened by a court on the ground that the interest charged is excessive.

items.head: Licensing of banking companies
items.gist: No company may carry on banking in India without a licence from the RBI; the RBI may cancel a licence; an aggrieved bank may appeal to the Central Government within 30 days.

items.head: Restrictions on opening of new, and transfer of existing, places of business
items.gist: Prior permission of the RBI is needed to open a new place of business or change its location.

items.head: Maintenance of a percentage of assets (SLR)
items.gist: Every bank must maintain liquid assets — cash, gold or unencumbered approved securities — of a percentage of its demand and time liabilities, as specified by the RBI.

items.head: Return of unclaimed deposits
items.gist: Banks must submit annual returns of accounts not operated for 10 years.

items.head: Depositor Education and Awareness Fund
items.gist: Amounts in accounts unclaimed for 10 years are transferred to the DEA Fund set up by the RBI; the depositor can still claim them.

items.head: Accounts and balance sheet
items.gist: Annual balance sheet and profit and loss account in the prescribed forms.

items.head: Audit
items.gist: Accounts audited by a qualified auditor; the RBI may order special audits.

items.head: Production of documents of confidential nature
items.gist: No court or tribunal may compel a bank to produce or give inspection of its books or documents claimed confidential relating to credit information, except as provided.

items.head: Inspection
items.gist: The RBI may at any time inspect any banking company and its books and accounts, and must on the Central Government's direction.

items.head: Power of the RBI to give directions
items.gist: In the public interest, in the interest of banking policy, of depositors or of proper management, the RBI may issue directions binding on banks.

items.head: Directions on stressed assets
items.gist: The Central Government may authorise the RBI to direct banks to initiate insolvency resolution in respect of a default, and the RBI may issue directions for resolving stressed assets.

items.head: Further powers and functions of the RBI
items.gist: Caution or prohibit particular transactions, assist amalgamations, require calling of meetings, appoint observers, and similar powers.

items.head: Power of the RBI to remove managerial and other persons
items.gist: The RBI may remove a chairman, director, chief executive officer or other officer and appoint a suitable person in his place.

items.head: Supersession of board of directors in certain cases
items.gist: The RBI may, after consulting the Central Government, supersede the board for up to 12 months and appoint an administrator.

items.head: Power of RBI to apply to Central Government for suspension of business and to prepare scheme of reconstruction or amalgamation
items.gist: The Central Government may order a moratorium on the RBI's application; the RBI may prepare a scheme of reconstruction or amalgamation with another bank.

items.head: Nomination for payment of depositors' money
items.gist: Depositors may nominate persons to receive the deposit on their death; payment to the nominee discharges the bank.

items.head: Nomination for return of articles kept in safe custody
items.gist: A person depositing articles for safe custody may nominate persons to whom they are returned on his death.

items.head: Release of contents of safety lockers
items.gist: A locker hirer may nominate persons; on the hirer's death the bank may give the nominee (or, for joint hirers, the survivor with the deceased's nominee) access to the locker and liberty to remove its contents, after an inventory.

items.head: Penalties
items.gist: Punishment for false statements, failure to produce books, accepting deposits in contravention of RBI orders, and other contraventions.

items.head: Power of RBI to impose penalty
items.gist: The RBI may impose monetary penalties on banks for contraventions, after giving an opportunity of being heard.

items.head: Restriction on acceptance of deposits withdrawable by cheque
items.gist: No person other than a banking company, the RBI, the SBI or other notified institution may accept deposits withdrawable by cheque.

items.head: Act to apply to co-operative societies subject to modifications
items.gist: The Act applies to co-operative banks with the modifications in S.56; since the 2020 amendment the RBI's control over co-operative banks (management, audit, reconstruction) is much wider.
